PNAS: Initialism of Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
PNEUMATIC: Of, relating to, or resembling air or other gases
PNEUMATICDRILL: A heavy drill consisting of a bit powered by compressed air, used e.g. for breaking tarmac.
PNEUMATICITY: The state of being pneumatic, or of having a cavity or cavities filled with air.
PNEUMATICS: The branch of mechanics that deals with the mechanical properties of gases
PNEUMATOPHORE: A gas-filled sac or float of some colonial marine coelenterates, such as the Portuguese man-of-war.
PNEUMOCOCCAL: Of, pertaining to or caused by a pneumococcus bacterium
PNEUMOCOCCIC: Of, pertaining to or caused by a pneumococcus bacterium.
PNEUMOCOCCUS: A gram-positive bacterium, Streptococcus pneumoniae, that causes pneumonia and other infectious diseases
PNEUMOCYTOSIS: pneumonia in people with impaired immune systems (typically as a result of AIDS)
PNEUMOGASTRIC: Of or pertaining to the lungs and the stomach
PNEUMONECTOMY: The surgical removal of all or part of a lung.
PNEUMONIA: Inflammation of the lungs caused by viruses, bacteria or other infectious microorganisms.
PNEUMONIC: Of, or relating to the lungs; pulmonary.
PNEUMONICPLAGUE: A severe lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis.
PNEUMONITIS: Inflammation of the tissue of the lungs.
PNEUMOTHORAX: Presence of air inside the pleural cavity, usually caused by injury either to the lung or the chest wall.
PNJUNCTION: An interface between a p-type and n-type semiconductor; used to create junction diodes and junction transistors
PNYX: A hill in Athens west of the Acropolis with a stone platform and steps set into its side, which was used as the meeting
